_comment: Per generated-artefact check: what verifies the artefact for its CONSUMER, as opposed to verifying that the committed copy is current. The two are different questions and the difference has cost six pages — library:viz:check was green while the page it generated could not run (PR #805). The check list is DERIVED from package.json and never listed here. Undeclared is a finding: 'nobody has said' is not 'nothing to check'. A `none` entry needs a REASON; an empty one looks decided and is not. This file may only SHRINK as entries move from `none` to `verified`; a declaration for a check that no longer exists is reported stale. `unchecked` (bean v556) is a second, independent inventory: scripts that WRITE a committed qa-results/v1 sidecar (they call the writer in qa-results.ts) and that no package.json command runs with --check, which the --check-derived list above structurally cannot contain. Each needs a reason or a --check.

verified.dc:render:check: folio-assistant-core/schemas/dublin-core-render.test.ts runs over the REAL catalogue records, not fixtures. For the JSON-LD's CONSUMERS: each document is expanded with jsonld.js through a loader that refuses every URL, so a rendering that needs a remote context to be read fails. In the expanded graph, every DCMI term whose range is a resource expands to a node carrying rdf:value and never to a bare literal; every source value appears exactly once under its field's predicate; MeSH subjects expand to a dcam:memberOf LINK to dcterms:MESH; dc.identifier.uri is typed dcterms:URI while govdoc stays off dcterms:identifier; and the subject @id expands to the item's Handle IRI. For the XML's CONSUMERS: each file is parsed and must be well-formed; the root declares dc, dcterms and xsi; only dc:/dcterms: elements and DCMI encoding schemes appear; every expressible value appears once; every inexpressible field is listed in a header comment; and markup in a value is escaped. NOT verified: validation against DCMI's own dcterms.xsd, which is not held locally, and whether a harvester accepts the container namespace.
verified.beans:notes:check: cat-harness/scripts/tests/bean-notes.test.ts, on scratch repositories with real branches: two branches adding notes to one bean on one day get disjoint paths and `git merge` exits 0; with the regenerated index committed too, the ONLY conflicted path is the index, it classifies as generated-regions, resolveGeneratedRegions resolves it, and the regenerated index lists both notes with the check clean. The check itself parses every note's front matter against BeanNoteFrontMatterSchema, re-derives its file name and requires its bean to exist. Not verified: that the index's Markdown renders on a site — beans/ is not published.
verified.bootstrap:vocabulary:check: bootstrap-tools/scripts/gen-vocabulary.test.ts, over the REAL bootstrap: the vocabulary holds every defined term in declared order and then every graph kind, and nothing else; it names nothing above bootstrap (no harness prefix in its context, no link out); its @id is the file's own path under the release, so publishing the file serves the namespace its IRIs name; and labels read as words. For its CONSUMER, the harness's full build: cat-harness/scripts/tests/ns-export-skos.test.ts asserts every bootstrap node the harness vocabulary holds IS bootstrap's file's node, node for node, so the two cannot drift; and ns-document-resolves.test.ts that both workflows publish the file at bootstrap's own IRI segment. Not verified: that the published address dereferences — nothing serves the bootstrap base until that repository publishes.
verified.iri:sync:check: bootstrap-tools/schemas/release-iri.test.ts: on a fixture base, a stale full version and a stale major are each moved to the declared one while the current ones stay, --from moves an old base's identifiers and leaves the bare base alone, and another base is never touched. Over the REAL declaration, bootstrap's release is composed from its iriBase and version. The consumers of the rewritten IRIs are covered where they read them: code-list.test.ts asserts each namespaces.ts constant equals its code list value, and graph.test.ts that every $schema a bootstrap file carries resolves to a bootstrap schema. Not verified: that an IRI dereferences — nothing serves the bootstrap base until that repository publishes.
verified.readme:subgraphs:check: scripts/tests/subgraph-readmes.test.ts: on fixture instances, a README is created holding only the kg:subgraph region, an existing region is replaced and the text around it kept, a README without markers is left untouched and reported, and every missing title, description or directory is a QA finding. Over the REAL tree, every link in every generated README resolves to a file. Not verified: whether a declared description is GOOD, which the long-description finding only measures by length.
verified.readme:sync:all:check: cat-harness/scripts/tests/readme-sections.test.ts, readme:toc block: the anchors a CONSUMER follows are asserted against GitHub's slug rule (punctuation dropped, spaces not collapsed, -1/-2 dedupe counted over every heading level, a literal x-1 bumped past), inline markup is stripped as GitHub renders it, headings inside code fences, HTML comments and indented code are excluded, the TOC's own region is not an input (a second sync is a no-op), and a heading another section generates is outlined on the same run. Not verified: that each anchor exists on the RENDERED page — readme:audit reports in-page anchors as not checked — and the other sections in these READMEs are verified only as far as readme:sync:check is.
verified.readme:sync:bootstrap:check: bootstrap-tools/schemas/graph.test.ts, over the REAL bootstrap/README.md: every relative link and image resolves to a file in bootstrap/ (the kg:processes pictures and every kg:files row), every link stays inside bootstrap/, and each term's drawing link reaches a heading that exists. The section CONTENT is checked separately by bootstrap-tools/scripts/readme-graph-sections.test.ts on fixture instances. Not verified here: that each picture is the CURRENT drawing of its diagram, which is render:bpmn:check's question.
verified.audit:coverage:check: audit-coverage.test.ts, over the LIVE corpus rather than a fixture — the consumer-side questions are about the artefact's content and not its currency, and all three are derived: every declared kind has exactly one row (`rows.length` against the registry plus instance-declared extras), every kind a gate declares is a kind that HAS a row (so an `@covers` typo cannot credit coverage to nothing), and each row's criteria are exactly those whose `applies` maps to that graph through `KG_SUBJECT_GRAPH_KINDS` (so a mis-attribution is caught rather than trusted). Plus the fixpoint assertion, which is a consumer question too: a reader who runs the writer once must get a file that agrees with the corpus. NOT verified by a runtime parse — `qa-results/v1` names a TypeScript shape (`scripts/qa-results.ts#QaResult`) rather than a Zod schema, so `check:kind-validators` reports it as could-not-determine and no `$schema` family validates it.
verified.check:glossary: folio-assistant-core/schemas/glossary.test.ts, over the REAL repository as well as fixtures. For the CONSUMERS of the SKOS: the scheme leads, every concept is skos:inScheme it, a concept's IRI is in the declaring instance's namespace, an exactMatch is emitted as a link and the external concept is never copied into the graph, members become a skos:Collection of external IRIs, a local broader resolves to the local IRI, and a candidate says so in skos:note. For the pages (split per asset type, owner 2026-09-24): there is an index and one page per asset type; every term appears exactly once across all the pages, on the page its scheme belongs to (authored on the index, extracted on its type's); each page is under its stated size budget (64 KB index, 1 MB per type, also enforced by the gate itself) and states it; the index links every per-type page and each links back; every page keeps the filter and the A–Z bar; and there is one SKOS file per scheme. For OWNERSHIP (owner 2026-09-24, "properly localed … no collision w/ other subgraphs"), over the real repository and computed independently of collect(): (a) no two schemes in any instance mint one scheme IRI; (b) no two instances resolve to one namespace; (c) every term with a repository source, authored and extracted alike, is minted in the namespace of the instance whose root holds that source (or of the instance its scheme's own source names as defining it, the extended-code-list case); and schemeOwner refuses a scheme sourced in several instances with no defining source rather than guessing. Each of (a), (b), (c) mutation-tested by hand, red. The schema's refusals are tested: an authored term with no definition, could-not-extract with no reason, a non-IRI match, a dangling broader, a duplicate id, an unknown key. For the EXTRACTED terms (bean lqo9, piece 1), over the real repository: every asset type contributes above a floor; every extracted term is a candidate whose source is a file in the repository and whose anchor names an element really in it; every definition is verbatim in its asset (a Tool's against the node, a skill's against its front matter, the rest against the file with entities decoded and comment markers dropped); a DMN decision is never defined by a rule's description; no two terms mint one IRI; an extracted IRI is in the namespace of the instance holding the asset; no term comes from roles.json or a lane; the pages mark every extracted row and schema.org, on the index only, carries authored terms only. Mutation-tested by hand, 13 mutations, each red. For a PAPER's glossary (bean lqo9, ruling 2, 2026-09-24), folio-assistant-core/scripts/build-glossary-skos.test.ts runs build-glossary.ts as a process over a fixture of two instances, root and sub, each with a paper of the same name: the scheme validates as folio-glossary/v1 and appears in collect() under its OWN instance (the sub-instance's for its paper, never the root's); status follows provenance (a definition block's term authored, a theorem's candidate, a term with no :defterm paragraph could-not-extract with its reason); the definition is the :defterm paragraph verbatim with directives replaced by their labels; no scheme or term IRI collides across the two instances and an authored scheme; glossary.json keeps its exact keys, so a downstream --check does not drift on upgrade; --check fails on a stale scheme and on a scheme id another document in the directory holds; and an instance with no glossary directory still passes. Mutation-tested by hand, each red. NOT verified: the same @context gap as glossary:check (`vigi`), and nothing dereferences an external concept IRI to prove it exists.
verified.check:harness-state:check: harness-state.test.ts, over the LIVE corpus. The consumer question for this sidecar is whether each family's verdict can be trusted, and that turns on the DENOMINATOR rather than on the shape: every family must have examined something or said it could not determine (a family at `examined: 0` with no reason is the filter-over-nothing this repository has paid for three times), family ids must be unique so two cannot collide in one sidecar, and the todo count must be less than double its items — `nodesOf` listed every file twice until 2026-09-24, because the repository root and `cat-harness` both resolve `todos` to `./todos`. The health family is additionally asserted to read `checkerHash()` rather than a re-derivation: the first version recomputed `sha256(run.ts)` and could never have passed, and a check that cannot pass is indistinguishable from a corpus that cannot be fixed. NOT verified by a runtime parse — `qa-results/v1` names a TypeScript shape, so no `$schema` family validates the file.
verified.check:library-qa:check: cat-harness/scripts/tests/check-library-qa.test.ts, over fixtures reproducing the defects measured on main (issue #1794). The consumer of this sidecar is a reviewer reading a finding as a fact about an entry, so the tests pin the judgements rather than the file: a slug or source file name is title-missing; a short token, a doubled word, a truncation and a Dublin Core record that disagrees are title-implausible, while extraction damage (hyphenation, case) is not; the DC record outranks the PDF Info /Title; a withheld entry's blocks are block-no-content with the reason while the same entry unwithheld is clean, and a heading-only section is not counted; and the three could-not-determine causes (an unparseable or undeclared-variant structure, a PDF source with no extraction) land there rather than reading as a pass. Each behaviour mutation-tested, one test red per mutation. Structure fixtures are REAL corpus structures of the right variant, edited, so they go through the schema accessor the script uses. NOT verified by a runtime parse: `qa-results/v1` names a TypeScript shape, so no `$schema` family validates the file.
verified.check:prov-qaqc: cat-harness/scripts/tests/prov-qaqc.test.ts, over fixtures and over the REAL repository. For the CONSUMERS of the PROV logs: every emitted record is parsed by ProvActivitySchema before it is written (a record that does not validate fails the gate), the agent, lane role, plan and policy of one mapped activity are asserted exactly, and a vacuity guard fails if the committed instances yield zero activities. For the report page: each finding kind (unknown, deny, not-eligible, undeclared actor, missing actor, unbound lane, disagreeing recorded authz, missing node) is produced from a fixture, and a missing actor or role is asserted to produce NO record rather than an invented one. Staleness and orphans are tested on a temporary site. NOT verified: nothing runs a JSON-LD processor over the logs, and nothing checks that a history entry is true, only that it is checked against the policy.
verified.kg:subscribe:check: cat-harness/scripts/tests/kg-subscribe.test.ts, over fixtures through the injectable fetcher: a valid substrate, a non-bootstrap declaration, zero harnesses, no or two root declarations, a fetch failure (could-not-determine, nothing written), an unpinned ref (refused before any fetch), and an idempotent re-subscribe. For the CONSUMER (the subscriptions visualizer, and slices 5-7 that read a snapshot's summary), --check re-hashes each snapshot's raw bytes against its sha256, re-judges those bytes with the same code that wrote the summary and fails on any difference, and holds every chosen subgraph and harness to what the substrate declares; each snapshot parses as folio-substrate-snapshot/v1. NOT verified: that the pinned commit still exists upstream, or that the substrate's declaration is TRUE of its own tree — --check never fetches.
verified.kg:materialize:check: folio-assistant-core/scripts/kg-materialize.test.ts, over fixtures through the injectable fetcher, and once live against litlfred/ihris at a real SHA in a scratch instance (2026-10-01, bytes not committed). For the CONSUMERS of a held part (check:materialized-fixity, the subscriptions page, slice 7): every record written is parsed by KgMaterializationRecordSchema before it lands, so its inner records are valid MaterializationSchema; the test runs check:materialized-fixity over a fixture checkout and asserts every held file is `verified`, the directory record `covered-by-parts`, and upstream's own materialization records inside tree/ are NOT read as ours; an edit in place fails both gates, and a file ADDED in place fails --check through the tree digest while the per-file walk stays green, which is why the digest exists. Refusals are asserted before any fetch (unchosen, undeclared, wrong policy, unsafe path), an unanswered gate keeps the part referenced with a record saying which, and a failed fetch writes nothing. NOT verified: that the pinned commit still exists upstream, or that a person's gate answers are TRUE — --check never fetches, and a gate is a decision it records rather than makes.
verified.subscriptions:viz:check: kg-subscriptions.test.ts and kg-instantiate.test.ts assert the RENDERED string: a chosen part with no materialisation record is drawn as not yet held, never as held; an empty registry says so rather than rendering an empty table; a chosen harness is drawn instantiated only once its `<name>.config.json` exists. The page is plain markdown tables with no inline script, so there is nothing to compile; what a consumer could be misled by is a state drawn wrongly, and that is what the tests pin. Materialised parts (slices 5+6): folio-assistant-core/scripts/kg-materialize.test.ts §"the subscriptions page draws a part from its record", over a fixture checkout with real records: a held, a gate-refused and a not-yet-held subgraph and a held asset each render their own state on their own row; bytes that no longer match render ⚠, never ⬇; and an unreadable record renders ? on its part's row rather than disappearing. NOT verified: that the page builds under Jekyll — the rows are a plain Markdown table, and docs:auto and the site build own rendering.
verified.check:remote-skills: cat-harness/scripts/tests/sync-remote-skills.test.ts and remote-skill-servable.test.ts. For the CONSUMER, skill_fetch: each synced skill is served as a local package with an entry point named after it. Every file's bytes are pinned by the sha256 in its materialization.json, which check:materialized-fixity re-hashes (an edit in place fails, probed 2026-09-24), and each record parses as folio-remote-skill/v1 in check:kind-validators. The record must name the wrapper's pinned commit and package. NOT verified: whether the upstream instructions are CORRECT. They are somebody else's, reviewed as a diff when the pin moves.
verified.check:term-mapping: cat-harness/scripts/tests/term-mapping.test.ts, over the LIVE glossary as well as fixtures. For the CONSUMER of the mapping result, not for its currency: every candidate gets a row for BOTH targets and the two counts agree, and — the load-bearing one — with no FHIR terminology in scope not a single row may read `unmapped`, only `undetermined` with a reason. That is the one way silence could be consumed as a negative answer (bean `dh4f`). The positive path is pinned on fixtures with deliberate collisions rather than on the corpus, because the corpus's honest answer today is 0 mapped and a check that always returns zero is indistinguishable from a broken one.
verified.check:viewer-nav: viewer-page.test.ts — and it verifies the CONSUMER's question rather than the file's currency. The consumer of this artefact is a reader who needs a way off the page, so the test asserts the two distinctions the verdict turns on: a declared opt-out is never read as an unwired page (either way round would let the fixture override a decision, or make an omission look deliberate), and a rail LOST is refused while a rail never present is only reported. The regression cases run on constructed verdict pairs, so they falsify the gate's own logic rather than today's tree; the audit cases run over a real temp docs tree including a Jekyll source page, which must not be counted at all. What is NOT verified here, deliberately: whether the rail's links resolve — they cannot be, from the source tree, because /who-iris/ and /smart-trust/ are mount routes created after Jekyll and /bootstrap/initialization.html is a .md Jekyll renders. check:subgraphs and the site-link tests own that against the built site.
verified.vocab-mappings:check: The tables' CONSUMERS are the generators that apply them and a FHIR consumer of the ConceptMaps they produce; both are verified where they read. glossary-export.test.ts runs buildGlossary over the REAL corpus through the real tables, and asserts that every key a table writes is bound in the document's @context to that table's target + code (27 rows), so a row cannot write one predicate while the context reads another; glossary-export's output was byte-identical before and after the move (bean k74z). vocab-mapping-fhir.test.ts pins the applier (a derived target sits after and copies its authoritative one; absent values write nothing; two rows writing one key is refused), asserts pi(iota(c)) = c on published HL7 R4 and R5 ConceptMaps with their sha256 pinned, that pi REPORTS each loss, and that what pi produces uses only element paths R5's StructureDefinition defines; and it pins this gate's own judgements (a derived target naming no authoritative one, an undeclared prefix) on constructed tables. NOT verified: a FHIR validator over a produced ConceptMap (none is held locally; the R5 path check is by shape only), and nothing runs a JSON-LD processor over the glossary output (`vigi`).
verified.code-lists:check: code-list.test.ts, over the REAL declared lists as well as fixtures. For the CONSUMERS: the engine test loads diagrams against the real lists and asserts it REFUSES a code the list does not define, a list nothing declares, and a list with no codes beside it — so a diagram that reads a list is checked where it reads it, at load, not by this gate's byte-free parse. For namespaces.ts: each exported constant is asserted equal to its code's value, and the JSON-LD scan is asserted to see external vocabularies and none of ours. The SKOS projection is asserted to mark a retired code owl:deprecated and to lead with the ConceptScheme. NOT verified: the same @context gap as glossary:check (`vigi`) — nothing runs a JSON-LD processor over <stub>-code-lists.jsonld.
verified.docs:auto:check: generated-viewer-scripts.test.ts — compiles every inline script in every generated viewer via `new Function`, which parses without executing. Derived over the whole generated tree, so a new viewer family is covered the day it is generated. This is the check that PR #805 proved was missing: library:viz:check was green while the page could not run.
verified.external-schemas:viz:check: external-schemas-viz.test.ts, and the half that matters runs over the REAL registry: every `](#id)` link in the summary table is resolved against the `<a id>` anchors the page carries, in BOTH the freshly rendered string and the committed file, so a record renamed or dropped fails here and not in a reader's browser (`pb04`). It also walks EVERY table on the page and pins each row's column count — `operative` is free prose across 53 terms and an unescaped pipe shifts every column to its right, rendering a table that is subtly wrong rather than obviously broken — and refuses to pass if that scan found fewer than ten rows, so a generator that stopped emitting tables cannot read as clean. The fixture half pins `classifyUsedBy`'s three states, including that a deliberate glob and a genuinely missing path stay distinguishable.
verified.folio:viz:check: folio-three-states.e2e.ts §"the folio viewer page RUNS" — six specs that LOAD the generated page in a browser and drive it against three projection states, which is the question a staleness check structurally cannot answer. It asserts no pageerror fires, that the row count equals the nodes in the real committed projection, and that the badge agrees with the rows it shows (tis1: a badge also makes a WRONG count visible). The three states are asserted apart because they are opposite facts the page must not render alike: a graph with nodes, an EMPTY graph ("not a graph that could not be read"), and a projection that 404s ("not an empty folio"). Plus folio-viz.test.ts, which asserts against the EMITTED string: the mount is present when the caller passes one and absent when it does not, the declared coverage.visualiser resolves to a file that exists (a declared path resolving to nothing is pb04 aimed at a declaration), and NO BACKTICK reaches the page — bmr0, which caught this author the same day in gen-library-viz. Written because this gate's own comment names the precedent: library:viz:check was green while the page it generated could not run (PR #805).
verified.glossary:check: glossary-export.test.ts, and it runs buildGlossary() over the REAL corpus rather than a fixture, so its assertions are about the emitted document: every live concept carries a prefLabel and no two share an @id; a concept's @id is the one kg-export already mints for that role, so the glossary does not fork the IRI space; notation is unique; every `usage` link resolves to a node in the same document; and the scheme is the document itself rather than a separate `…#scheme` IRI that would not dereference (`blv9`). The ledger half is covered separately — retirement, un-retirement, firstSeen preserved across a rebuild, and a wrong $schema REFUSED rather than overwritten. NOT verified: nothing dereferences the @context or runs a real JSON-LD processor over the output — the graph is JSON-LD by convention rather than by construction, which is bean `vigi`.
verified.glossary:pot:check: folio-assistant-core/scripts/glossary-pot.test.ts, over the REAL repository. For the CONSUMER (a translator): the templates hold EXACTLY the authored terms' prefLabel, altLabel and definition in the source language, with a floor (at least 7 authored terms, at least 14 msgids) so an empty glossary cannot pass; no candidate or could-not-extract text is a msgid, over more than a thousand candidates; no extracted scheme has a template; each authored term's IRI is its label's translator comment, once; and the committed .pot in every locale (ar, es, fr, ru, zh) carries that same set. A fixture scheme mixing the three states yields the authored term only. Mutation-tested by hand: candidates admitted, definitions dropped, each red. NOT verified: per-locale rendering of the glossary page, which reads no .po yet (the next step in bean lqo9).
verified.id-lookup:check: cat-harness/schemas/id-lookup.test.ts and cat-harness/test/id-lookup.e2e.ts, for the CONSUMER, a reader resolving an identifier. Over the COMMITTED index: every referenced who-iris node, counted from the raw catalogue independently of the build, resolves through the shards using the client a browser runs (lookup.js), including input in upper case with whitespace; a materialised node is absent; every shard parses, is listed in the manifest and is under the 64 KiB budget. In Chromium against the test server: every referenced node resolves from the real page with at most one shard requested per lookup, and the form links a found node to where it is held and says when one is absent. At scale, 60,000 synthetic IRIS-shaped items: every id resolves with exactly one shard fetched, no shard exceeds the budget, and the chosen prefix length is the smallest that fits. Staleness: a changed, a missing and a stale shard are each reported. Vacuity: an empty selection is refused. Mutation-tested by hand, 7 mutations plus 2 on the CLI, each red. NOT verified: nothing publishes the page yet, so no gate loads it from the deployed site.
verified.ingest:ig-chrome:check: ig-chrome.test.ts over the SCHEMA and the resolver, ingest-ig-chrome.test.ts over the OVERLAY, and pages-markdown.test.ts over the rendered result. 28 tests, all on synthetic layers rather than the real template checkouts, which are on no runner. The overlay tests pin the three facts a flat stylesheet cannot carry: the last layer wins and the shadowed value is RECORDED; `overrides: []` means exactly one layer decided a token, which is what attributes the yellow publish box to HL7 rather than WHO; and a lower layer declaring the IDENTICAL value is not an override, without which that attribution would be meaningless. Both upstream defect detectors are pinned in both directions -- the `--toc-box-border` shape conflict and the `##555555` malformation fire, and agreeing or well-formed layers raise nothing, because a false positive here accuses somebody else's published stylesheet of a fault it does not have. `ruleFor` is asserted on the ABSENT case specifically, since present-vs-absent is the whole of the attribution. For the consumer -- a reader looking at a page that claims to mirror the WHO IG -- the verification is `smart-trust:pages:check`: all 681 pages are regenerated FROM chrome.json and compared byte for byte, so chrome that changed upstream and chrome that failed to parse both fail the gate rather than quietly serving unstyled pages that still say they are a mirror. pages-markdown.test.ts additionally asserts that NO page emits a bare `:root`, which is the rule that makes mirroring a third party's palette safe at all. KNOWN GAP, stated rather than assumed: nothing renders these pages and compares them to the published WHO IG. `smart.who.int` and the gh-pages mirror both answer 403 CONNECT from this environment, so a visual diff cannot run here, and the values are ingested verbatim from three named commits rather than matched by eye -- right by construction rather than by comparison. Bean `ajx9`.
verified.ingest:ig-menu:check: ig-menu.test.ts over the PARSE and the join, plus pages-markdown.test.ts over the RENDERED result. `groupsFromSushiMenu` is asserted on both of SUSHI's two menu shapes (a nested map and a bare string) and on file order, because the top bar's order IS the config's order and alphabetising it would silently re-navigate the IG. `menuHref` is asserted on the double-slash cases from both sides, since a broken link in a navigation bar is a defect a reader meets before any test does. For the consumer — a reader using the left-hand nav — the verification is `smart-trust:pages:check`: the 5 section pages are regenerated FROM menu.json and compared byte for byte, so a menu that changed upstream and a menu that failed to parse both fail the gate rather than quietly emptying the sidebar. KNOWN GAP, stated rather than left to be assumed: nothing resolves the 29 hrefs. They point at pages the IG publishes and this repository does not hold, and both `smart.who.int` and the gh-pages mirror answer 403 CONNECT from this environment, so a link check cannot run here. The hrefs are ingested verbatim from `sushi-config.yaml` at a recorded commit rather than composed, which is what makes them right by construction instead of by testing.
verified.kg:locale:check: kg-locale-export.test.ts, and the coverage is UNEVEN in a way worth stating. translateDocument's assertions run over a fixture, not the real graph: a translated value carries its own @language tag, an untranslated string falls through plain and untagged, the document declares the SOURCE language rather than the locale, every @id stays the core's, identity-bearing keys and links are never rewritten even on a msgid hit, and the core document is not mutated. Only three tests run over the real graph — that there are locales to report on, that every locale is reported whether emitted or not, and localeDocumentsUnreferenced()'s four banned shapes over the committed core, which is the one consumer-facing invariant checked against what is actually shipped. The mutation that proves the IRI-protection test is not vacuous is in the fixture set. NOT verified: the same @context gap as glossary:check (`vigi`), and no check that a committed per-locale document's @ids still resolve after the core moves.
verified.library:viz:check: generated-viewer-scripts.test.ts — compiles every inline script in every generated viewer via `new Function`, which parses without executing. Derived over the whole generated tree, so a new viewer family is covered the day it is generated. This is the check that PR #805 proved was missing: library:viz:check was green while the page could not run.
verified.methodologies:viz:check: methodologies-viz.test.ts, and the half that matters runs over the REAL corpus rather than a fixture: every `](#name)` link in the page's selection table is resolved against the `<a id>` anchors the page itself carries, in BOTH the freshly rendered string and the committed file — so a link to a section that was renamed or dropped fails here, not in a reader's browser (`pb04`). It also pins the column count of every table row, because `origin` and `applies-when` are free prose and one of them already contains a pipe: an unescaped one shifts every column to its right and renders a table that is subtly WRONG rather than obviously broken. The fixture half pins the join — which of the three evidence states a node lands in, keyed by node PATH rather than by name, since two instances may adopt methods one letter apart.

The load-bearing one converts the generated `rem` back to px and asserts it equals `navbar-geometry.ts`'s own constant for collapsed/open/mark: the question the artefact exists to answer, which a byte comparison cannot ask.
